primary_secondary.note: Author's own framework (Knowledge Activation) plus Yahoo deployment and survey (n = 67).

gl_type.note: arXiv pre-print, not peer reviewed; author employed by Yahoo, where the framework was deployed.

dora_applied.note: DORA 2025 report cited for the AI productivity paradox.

space_applied.note: SPACE discussed in background and recommended for future measurement.

ai_discussed.note: Knowledge delivery for agentic AI software development (AI skills for coding agents).

remote_covid.note: Neither mentions remote work or COVID-19.

data_window.note: Only Claude states the survey dates; NotebookLM gives no data period.

cat_productivity.note: Self-reported time saved per week (mean 2.6 h); knowledge density (task-completion value per token) proposed.

cat_quality.note: Borderline: only perceived first-try policy compliance (Likert) and proposed correction frequency/agent accuracy; no code quality measure.

cat_collaboration.note: Institutional knowledge and the senior 'knowledge tax' are conceptual; no collaboration or knowledge-sharing metric measured.

cat_satisfaction.note: Net Promoter Score (+35) and perceived developer-experience improvements.

cat_activity.note: 68 merged PRs to the skill corpus are only descriptive deployment statistics (Claude).

cat_devex.note: Borderline: DevEx (cognitive load) justifies the intervention and the survey asks about mental effort and flow, but both extractions treat DevEx as referenced; drivers are the author's own items.

cat_survey.note: Anonymous cross-sectional Likert survey of 67 engineers (40 active users).

evidence.quote: The bottleneck to effective agentic software development is not model capability but knowledge architecture.

statistically significant developer-experience improvements (large to very large effect sizes on all four perceived-experience drivers, a mean of 2.6 hours per week saved per engineer, a Net Promoter Score of +35
To assess the deployment's effect on developer experience, we fielded an anonymous, online cross-sectional survey of Yahoo engineers between May 1 and May 15, 2026.
We computed bootstrap confidence intervals for the Net Promoter Score with 10,000 resamples.
Active users reported saving a mean of 2.6 hours per week (95% CI: 1.6-3.6 hours)
